questions.question: What does MCP stand for in the Claude developer ecosystem?
questions.explanation: MCP means Model Context Protocol. It defines a standardized way for applications to connect AI systems with external tools and context sources through MCP clients and servers.

questions.question: An agent repeatedly calls a tool with the same invalid arguments. What is a good design improvement?

options.text: Return actionable validation errors and bound retries with clear stopping conditions
Hide all tool errors from the model

questions.explanation: Structured errors can help the model correct its arguments. Retry limits, validation, and explicit stopping conditions prevent loops, excessive cost, and repeated unsafe actions.

questions.question: Before invoking a newly discovered MCP tool, what should a secure client do?

options.text: Inspect its description and schema, validate arguments, and apply authorization policy
Assume every tool is safe because it uses MCP
Send all available secrets to the tool

questions.explanation: MCP standardizes communication, not trustworthiness. Clients should evaluate tool metadata, validate inputs, enforce least privilege, and apply approval requirements for sensitive actions.

questions.question: A tool accepts a file path supplied by Claude. Which control is most important?

options.text: Restrict access to approved directories and validate the resolved path
Trust the path because the model generated it
Run every file operation as an administrator

questions.explanation: Model-generated arguments are untrusted input. Resolve paths safely, prevent traversal outside permitted locations, and apply operating-system permissions and application authorization.
